# aiLr Workspace Notes

- Backend source is under `backend/`; run its tests with `python -m unittest discover -s backend/tests -v` from the workspace root.
- `backend/app/settings.py` is the single source of truth for Lightroom develop controls: `DEVELOP_CONTROLS` / `develop_controls_payload()` drive the web UI (`GET /api/develop/controls`), the model JSON schema, the MCP tools and the bridge whitelist. Add a parameter there, then mirror it in `Bridge.lua`'s `SETTING_KEYS` (and `CONTROLLER_ALIASES` when the `LrDevelopController` name differs).
- `MODEL_SETTING_KEYS` is the default set the vision model may adjust (every non `experimental` control, value kinds `number` / `enum` / `bool` / `curve` included). The web UI keeps a per-parameter "allowed for the model" switch (default on for non experimental controls) and posts it as the `allowed_keys` form field of `POST /api/suggestions`; `model_keys_for()` intersects it with the registry, and `llm.py` builds the prompt plus JSON schema per request and drops anything the caller disallowed. Turning a switch off must never write a default value, so the panel row carries a separate `＋` button that adds the control to the current render. `_model_default()` / the payload's `model_default` field is the default state of that switch: every non experimental control except the mask, which is `VIGNETTE_SETTING_KEYS` (the five `PostCropVignette*` keys, also exposed as `mask_keys`) and ships switched off behind the single 蒙版 switch plus its 关闭/轻/中/强 strength presets at the top of the 参数微调 block (they write -15 / -30 / -50 with feather 60, roundness 0, midpoint 50, style 1). Turning the mask off also removes the vignette keys from the current render, so the switch state and the values sent to the bridge never disagree.
- The instruction prompt in `llm.py` is role + working method + output contract (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_ROLE` / `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CRAFT` / `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CONTRACT`), followed by the per-request allowed key lists. It states that only global develop sliders can be written (no masks, no local adjustments, no crop, no healing brush); keep that claim in sync if the bridge ever gains local editing.
- Model answers can overflow the registry (number outside its range, unknown enum value, wrong JSON type). `settings.review_develop_settings()` returns `(accepted, problems)` instead of raising; `llm.py` sends `problems` back to the model as the next user turn (`MAX_PARAMETER_REPAIR_ROUNDS`, default 2), drops whatever still fails, and returns an `overflow` block (`notice` / `resolved` / `unresolved` / `dropped_keys`) that the web UI shows above the parameter list. `validate_develop_settings()` stays the strict single-answer path for the bridge and MCP. Nothing outside the validated values may reach Lightroom.
- Lightroom's Post Crop vignette is the only control that can draw a shape the eye reads as a region of the photo, so the suggestion path guards it too: `settings.VIGNETTE_SAFE_WINDOW` (amount +/-60, midpoint 20-80, feather >= 25, roundness <= 25, never style 3) is reported by `review_develop_settings(..., guard_vignette=True)` and enforced by `tame_vignette_artifacts()` right before the answer is returned; the `overflow` block carries the per-change notes in `adjusted`. Only the model path turns this on - the web sliders, the bridge and the MCP keep sending hand-made values exactly as given. `llm.py` appends the `VIGNETTE_RULE` paragraph (and its window) to the system prompt only when a vignette key is in the allowed set, so the mask stays invisible to the model while the switch is off.
- The MCP server uses the official Python SDK v2 (`mcp>=2`). Reference: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/ and https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/build-server.
- MCP stdio output is reserved for protocol messages; send diagnostic logs to stderr.
- The Lightroom Classic plugin bridge writes develop settings back through `LrDevelopController` and reports per-parameter rejections to `POST /api/lightroom/jobs/{id}/report`; keep the plug-in failure path split between "some parameters rejected" (warning, render continues) and "everything rejected" (failed job).
